title: Sacramento Husband Said ICE Took His Wife; He Is Now Charged With Her Murder
excerpt: Gurinder Gill, 28, told detectives ICE had detained his wife Jasmine Gill, 30, while she checked the mail. ICE said no agents were ever at the home; her burned remains were found in El Dorado County, and he was arrested on October 14.
body:
• Gurinder Gill, 28, has been charged with the murder of his wife, Jasmine Gill, 30, an India-born nurse whose burned remains were found in El Dorado County on October 1 — a day after she was last seen at the couple's Sacramento home.
  • Gill told detectives that ICE agents had taken his wife into custody while she was checking the mail. ICE confirmed to the Sacramento County Sheriff's Office that no enforcement activity occurred at the residence.
  • Detectives say they found inconsistencies in Gill's statements; the couple was in an ongoing divorce and child custody dispute. He was arrested on October 14 and is held without bail.
  • Jasmine Gill leaves an 8-month-old son. Her family has organised a fundraiser to return her remains to India and support the child — details below. If you or someone you know is experiencing domestic violence in the US, the National Domestic Violence Hotline is 1-800-799-7233.

A Sacramento husband who told detectives that immigration agents had taken his wife has been charged with her murder. Gurinder Gill, 28, was arrested on October 14 after burned human remains discovered in neighbouring El Dorado County were confirmed to be those of his wife, Jasmine Gill, 30, the Sacramento County Sheriff's Office said. He is booked into Sacramento County Main Jail on a murder charge and is ineligible for bail. He has not been convicted, and the allegations have not been tested in court.

Jasmine Gill was an India-born registered nurse and the mother of an 8-month-old boy. She was last seen at the couple's Sacramento residence on September 30.

The ICE Claim — and How It Unravelled

Her cousin reported her missing on October 4. During the initial investigation, according to the sheriff's office statement, Gurinder Gill claimed that Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents had taken Jasmine into custody while she was checking the mail at their residence. Detectives contacted ICE, which confirmed that no enforcement activity had occurred at the residence.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=9mDdfA6l0HY

"As the investigation progressed, Sacramento County Sheriff's Office detectives identified several inconsistencies in Gurinder's statements about his wife's disappearance."

— Sgt. Edward Igoe, Sacramento County Sheriff's Office

Detectives also learned that the couple was engaged in an ongoing divorce and child custody dispute. On October 1 — three days before Jasmine was reported missing — burned human remains had been discovered in El Dorado County, roughly 70 miles east of Sacramento. Investigators linked jewellery found with the remains to Jasmine, a sheriff's spokesperson told KCRA, and the remains were confirmed as hers. Homicide detectives obtained an arrest warrant, arrested Gill on October 14, and executed search warrants at two residences associated with him. He was arraigned the following Friday, according to the Sacramento Bee via PEOPLE.

What Authorities Have Not Said

The sheriff's office has released no cause of death, no motive, and no account of where the alleged killing took place. Coverage by Fox News and other outlets notes the charge alleges the killing occurred on or about September 30, the day Jasmine was last seen. The investigation remains active.

https://x.com/ICEgov/status/2113388554172678596

A Family Raising Funds to Bring Her Home

Jasmine's family has organised a GoFundMe campaign — "Bring Jasmine's Body Home, Seek Justice," organised by family member Daman Gill — to return her remains to India for funeral rites with her mother, support her 8-month-old son, and cover legal costs around the child's custody and welfare. The campaign had raised more than $21,000 as of October 20. "She was fighting for a better future for herself and her baby," the campaign says. "She was seeking a divorce. She was trying to find the freedom, safety, and fresh start they both deserved." Readers who wish to help can find the family's verified campaign on GoFundMe under that title.

The case has drawn attention because the false ICE claim played on a fear that is real in immigrant communities in 2026. Detectives' work — checking the claim against ICE's own records — is what exposed it. If you or someone you know is experiencing domestic violence, the National Domestic Violence Hotline — 1-800-799-7233 — is free, confidential and available around the clock.

Correction: an earlier version of this article, published October 22, carried incorrect names, ages and dates drawn from faulty source research. The facts above are taken from the Sacramento County Sheriff's Office statement and corroborating US coverage. We regret the error.
nri_angle: An India-born nurse in Sacramento was killed and her husband allegedly blamed an ICE detention that never happened; her family is raising funds to bring her remains home to India and support her infant son.
